tutor_message.content: A useful concept in this problem is how linked lists can be traversed and rearranged by reassigning node pointers, rather than creating new nodes or using extra storage. Think about how you can maintain references to the heads and tails of both the "odd" and "even" portions as you iterate through the list, so you can reconnect them efficiently at the end while preserving their original relative order.

{"conversation":"Ok, so I think I need to keep track of two pointers, one for odd nodes and one for even nodes, and then connect the odd list to the even list at the end. I'll try making two pointers, odd and even, that start at the first and second nodes respectively and then iterate through the list, updating next pointers accordingly.","python_code":"class Solution:
    def oddEvenList(self, head: Optional[ListNode]) -> Optional[ListNode]:
        if not head:
            return head
        
        odd = head
        even = head.next
        even_head = even
        
        while even and even.next:
            odd.next = even.next
            odd = odd.next
            even.next = odd.next
            even = even.next
        
        odd.next = even_head
        return head"}
